A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of very strongly disturbed metal films can be described by the concept of solid solutions, and that the resistivity of such films is determined by the concentration of defects and by the concentration of impurities.
the resistivity of films is not determined by their crystallite sizes, as is generally assumed, but rather by the degree of order in the lattice.
, in the case of copper, there is a transition at a critical temperature, below which the film is amorphous and above which the film is polycrystalline.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the substrate temperature is the key to obtaining solid solutions.
